prompt_en:
Goal: Create a square comparison sheet showing two different storybook-style image generations from the same rainy dragon prompt, with the top half labeled as a warm red-raincoat version and the bottom half as a hydrangea-blue rainy version.

Canvas: Square 1:1 white background, like a clean social media comparison post. Divide the canvas into two horizontal halves separated by a centered Japanese caption line. Use hand-drawn panel borders with slightly uneven ink lines and softly rounded corners.

Top section: Label the upper-right corner in small red handwritten text: “Nano Banana2”. Arrange exactly 3 panels: 1 wide rectangular panel at upper left showing a child in a red raincoat struggling with a beige umbrella in heavy wind and rain, with dark storm clouds and bent trees; 1 wide rectangular panel below it showing a side-profile child in the same red raincoat holding the umbrella against a mostly blank white background; 1 large tall rounded rectangular panel on the right showing a friendly orange dragon bending down under the rain toward the child in a red hooded raincoat, the dragon’s wings forming a warm shelter-like shape. The child’s face may be softly blurred or simplified. Use warm orange, red, and ochre as the dominant colors.

Center caption: Add one centered line of small Japanese text between the halves: “ともに温かみのある、絵本のようなイラストという指定”.

Bottom section: Label the lower-left corner in small pastel purple handwritten text: “GPT Image2”. Arrange exactly 3 panels: 1 small panel at bottom-left top showing a little girl in a yellow raincoat standing in heavy rain under a blue umbrella, surrounded by wet pavement, streetlamp glow, and purple-blue hydrangeas; 1 small panel directly beneath it showing the same girl looking upward with a small white question mark near her head; 1 large wide panel on the right showing the girl smiling up at a gentle white-blue dragon in the rain, with the dragon lowering its head toward her and spreading a translucent wing, hydrangeas blooming on both sides, reflections on the wet ground, and a magical blue twilight atmosphere.

Subject details: The main child is a young child or little girl; the top outfit is red hooded raincoat; the bottom outfit is yellow raincoat with blue skirt; the dragon theme is orange dragon above and white-blue dragon below; the weather theme is heavy rain during the rainy season with hydrangeas.

Visual style: Warm children’s picture book illustration, watercolor and colored pencil texture, soft ink outlines, visible brush granulation, gentle expressions, cinematic rain streaks, cozy emotional storytelling. Top half feels windy, warm, and orange-red; bottom half feels moist, luminous, blue-purple, and hydrangea-themed.

Constraints: Use exactly 6 illustrated panels total, exactly 2 model labels, and exactly 1 centered Japanese caption line. Do not add extra UI, logos, watermarks, or additional text. Keep the composition readable as a side-by-side model comparison sheet.\

3. Middle-left panel: Similar stalking perspective from behind the observer on the left foreground, closer to her shoulder and hair. The main subject is far ahead in the center of the street, walking away through the wet reflections and crowd.

Goal: Create a vertical 4:5 macro-detail scientific plate infographic about White-Spotted Pufferfish, presenting the animal as a dramatic full-bleed reef landscape with an information-rich magazine layout.

Canvas: Portrait 4:5 aspect ratio, dark teal oceanic background, high-resolution photorealistic macro wildlife photography blended with clean vector infographic panels. Use cream, sand, muted yellow, aqua, and coral-orange accents. Add subtle bubbles, reef texture, and rounded panel borders.

Main subject: A large photorealistic white-spotted pufferfish, Arothron hispidus, centered slightly low and right, facing right, inflated into a round body covered in dense white spots, with a glossy yellow-ringed eye, small puckered mouth, translucent fins, and coral reef visible behind it. The fish should dominate the center like a landscape specimen.

Top title area: Large condensed uppercase cream headline reading WHITE-SPOTTED PUFFERFISH. Under it, add the italic yellow scientific name “Arothron hispidus”, then a small taxonomy line “Actinopterygii / Tetraodontiformes / Tetraodontidae” and a short description: “A charismatic coral reef resident with powerful defenses and a slow-moving demeanor—cute, clever, and potentially deadly.”

Left column: Create a vertical panel titled “DEFENSIVE FEATURES” with exactly 6 numbered feature cards, each with a small photo crop and text. The 6 cards are: 1) “INFLATION” showing an inflated pufferfish face, explaining it rapidly fills its stomach with water or air to swell into a large rounded ball; 2) “SPINES” showing close-up raised sharp skin spines, explaining they erect from the skin when inflated; 3) “TOUGH SKIN” showing leathery spotted skin, explaining thick skin in bumps and scales provides mechanical protection; 4) “BEAK-LIKE TEETH” showing the mouth, explaining fused powerful teeth crush hard-shelled prey like crabs, snails, and urchins; 5) “TOXIN RISK” showing the pufferfish with a biohazard symbol and yellow warning triangle, explaining tetrodotoxin can be lethal and has no antidote; 6) “WARNING POSTURE” showing a fully inflated spiny fish, explaining the threatened animal inflates, raises spines, and displays bold contrast patterns.

Right column: Create stacked rounded science panels. At the top, a taxonomy card with exactly 3 rows and icons: “CLASS: Actinopterygii (ray-finned fishes)”, “ORDER: Tetraodontiformes (pufferfishes and relatives)”, and “FAMILY: Tetraodontidae (true pufferfishes)”. Below it, a “RANGE” panel with a beige world map on teal and orange highlighted Indo-Pacific distribution, captioned “Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Australia, and east to French Polynesia.” Below, create exactly 3 ecological cards: “PREDATORS” with shark, grouper, moray eel, and seabird imagery; “DIET” with crab, snail, and sea urchin imagery; and “BEHAVIOR” with a small pufferfish portrait, describing slow relaxed movement, often hovering near reefs, solitary or paired, not aggressive unless provoked.

Center-lower info strip: Add a small “HABITAT” card near the fish with a coral icon and text about coral reefs and lagoons in clear tropical waters, usually near slopes and sheltered areas from the surface down to 40 meters. Along the bottom of the central area, add exactly 5 metric tiles with icons: “SIZE Up to 50 cm (20 in)”, “WEIGHT Up to 2.5 kg (5.5 lb)”, “SPEED Up to 8 km/h (5 mph)”, “LIFESPAN 10–15 years in the wild”, and “CONSERVATION STATUS LEAST CONCERN (LC), IUCN Red List”.

Bottom section: Create two large rounded panels. Left panel titled “KEY ADAPTATIONS” with exactly 7 green check bullet points: elastic stomach for rapid inflation; spines that erect via muscular control; tough spined skin for physical defense; powerful beak for crushing hard prey; tetrodotoxin as chemical defense; excellent camouflage with white spots blending into coral and sand; strong pectoral fins for precise maneuvering. Include a circular inset image of a spiny inflated pufferfish. Right panel titled “3 SURPRISING FACTS” with exactly 3 numbered facts: 1) they can “walk” on the seafloor using pectoral fins; 2) tetrodotoxin is not produced by the fish itself but comes from bacteria in its diet and varies by location and season; 3) despite their slow look, they are excellent problem-solvers with good memory. Add three small supporting illustrations: walking pufferfish, green bacterium, and blue brain.

Footer: Add a narrow rounded banner with a camera icon and the conservation message Admire, don’t take. Photograph, don’t touch. These amazing defenses belong in the ocean. followed by a small blue heart.

Constraints: Use exactly the listed panel counts and numbered items. Keep all text in English, legible, and aligned to a polished educational poster grid. Avoid extra animals or unrelated labels. No watermark, no QR code, no logos.\

Panel layout and count: Use exactly 4 panels.
1. Top panel: Wide action shot. The coffee worker rides the armored dinosaur down the street, looking confused and searching himself while holding the kettle. The dinosaur roars with mouth open. Add a small red-and-white mushroom floating above them as a whimsical detail. Include one large white speech bubble on the left with Japanese text: 「あれ？スマホどこだ？」

Layout: Arrange exactly 35 visible map thumbnails in an irregular grid. Count them as: 8 small thumbnails across the top row, 10 large landscape thumbnails in the middle two rows, 12 smaller portrait/landscape thumbnails in the lower middle arranged in paired columns, and 5 large purple-themed thumbnails along the bottom row. Include several partially cropped thumbnails on the far right edge to imply the board continues off-screen.

Thumbnail content: Each thumbnail is a different failed variation of a futuristic world map for United Federation of Valoria. Most maps show altered Earth-like continents but not an accurate real-world map. Use dark navy or black ocean backgrounds, neon blue coastlines, cyan glowing borders, faint green landmasses, satellite-map textures, grid overlays, small HUD-like ticks, and occasional white title text. Some thumbnails should look like color tests: one bright blue-and-yellow terrain map, one simple black-outline map on white, and multiple glowing cyberpunk versions. The bottom row should use a different purple faction label, Empathia Union, with purple-highlighted landmasses around Eurasia/Australia-like shapes.

Visible labels: Repeat the title text on many thumbnails, usually centered or near the lower third, reading United Federation of Valoria. Vary the typography and size slightly so some labels are tiny, misaligned, or awkwardly placed. Bottom-row thumbnails should instead read Empathia Union. A few labels may be partially illegible due to scale, cropping, or glow.

Visual style: Make it look like a collection of generated image results, not a polished infographic. Use inconsistent map compositions, inconsistent coastline shapes, different zoom levels, different title placements, and slightly mismatched aspect ratios. The dominant palette is black, deep navy, electric cyan, blue, green, and purple, with occasional white thumbnails and one or two bright terrain-map thumbnails.
